tei:titleStmt.tei:title: Ketoret: Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel says: “The balm is nothing but sap

tei:availability.tei:p: Published by Sefaria under CC-BY, which Sefaria defines as Creative Commons Attribution 3.0.

tei:div.tei:p: Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel says: “The balm is nothing but sap which drips from the balsam tree. Why was the Carshina lye used? To refine the onycha in order to make it pleasant. Why was Cyprus wine used? The onycha was soaked in it to give it a pungent odor. Though the water of Raglayim was well suited for that purpose, they did not bring the water of Raglayim into the Temple because it would be disrespectful.

tei:note.tei:p: 10 This water came from a well named Raglayim.—Kol Bo

Since Mei Raglayim (lit., water from the feet) is a euphemism for urine, it would have been disrespectful to use this water in the Temple. Others hold that the term “waters of Raglayim” actually refers to urine, which could have been used as a soaking agent were it not indecent to bring it into a sacred place.—Kol Bo
